fields.rationale: States cluster around whether they require documented active practice hours, whether they focus primarily on equivalency of the other state's standards, whether a jurisprudence exam is a distinct centerpiece, whether reciprocity is expressly restricted or only available via special pathways, or whether the state relies on a compact or portability program — these axes capture the main structural differences across the raw values.

assignments.raw_value: Active license from another state or territory, proof of continued competence, payment of required fee, in-person interview with board

Active practice for 5 years or 5,000 hours; current valid unrevoked license in a state with equivalent examination standards; in good standing without restrictions; not subject to pending disciplinary action; passes jurisprudence exam; and meets other board criteria.

Applicant must have practiced continuously for five or more years under a license lawfully issued by another state, territory, DC, or Canada where the standard of proficiency at least equals that of Arkansas; must submit original or certified copy of license, certificate from issuing authority, and fee.

Board may waive examination requirements if applicant passed clinical exam of another state or testing agency (even more than 5 years before application) and that state maintains substantially equivalent standards. Requires minimum active practice hours, affirmation of CE completion in jurisdiction of licensure, and payment of a fee of not more than $2,000.

Active and unrestricted out-of-state license; at least 5 years active clinical practice (or full-time nonclinical practice requiring active dentist license, or full-time faculty with 5,000 hours clinical practice); no disciplinary history; NPDB release; no failed exam within 5 years (unless subsequently passed); 50 units of CE within 2 years; additional board requirements.

Applicant must satisfy the requirements of the occupational credential portability program (§ 12-20-202(3)), including proof of substantially equivalent experience or credentials, good standing in another state, payment of fees, and compliance with any other applicable requirements.

Applicant must hold a current valid license in good professional standing from another state or territory with commensurate standards (except practical examination) and must have worked continuously as a licensed dentist in an academic or clinical setting in another state or territory for at least one year immediately preceding the application. No license issued if disciplinary action is pending or unresolved complaint exists. Fee of $565.

Applicant must present proof of current licensure in good standing in another state/DC/territory; maintain license in good standing; satisfy character and background requirements; for dentists: CODA-accredited degree plus 3 years active dental practice in another jurisdiction; for dental hygienists: 3 of last 5 years active practice plus required exams; must also have remained academically current through continuing education.

Licensure by endorsement available under the MOBILE Act (s. 456.0145) and by health access dental license pathway (s. 466.0067). For health access dental license: must hold valid active out-of-state license, submit proof of ADLEX or equivalent clinical exam, have 5 years of active clinical practice, pass FL laws/rules exam, meet CE requirements, and practice only in health access settings.

Must hold active dental license in good standing from another state; must have been in full-time clinical practice or full-time faculty for 5 years preceding application; must have passed a clinical examination by a state or regional testing agency approved by the board; must pass a jurisprudence examination; must hold a D.D.S. or D.M.D. from a CODA-accredited school approved by the board.

Community service license available without examination for practitioners holding active unrestricted dental practice license from another state who meet eligibility criteria; military spouse licensure by endorsement also available.

License by credentials (without examination) requires: (1) license from another state with equivalent requirements; (2) either passage of a regional or national examination approved by the dental board OR three consecutive years of legal practice in that other state immediately prior to application; (3) other evidence of qualifications as the board may require. Interstate compact privileges also available.

Applicant must hold an active license in good standing in another state with no disciplinary proceedings; have been in clinical practice at least 5 years for a minimum of 3,500 hours; graduated from a CODA-accredited dental school; completed national board dental examinations; completed a board-approved clinical examination; and paid the application fee.

Applicant must have been lawfully licensed in another state with substantially equivalent requirements, practiced dentistry for at least 2 years immediately preceding application, and deposit a duly attested certificate from the board of the state in which licensed. 'Substantially equivalent' means graduation from an ADA-accredited dental college, passing both parts of the National Board Dental Examination, and completing a regional testing service examination.

Applicant must be licensed in another state or Canadian province with substantially equal requirements, have practiced dentistry for at least two of the three years preceding application, pass the law examination, and have completed required continuing education hours in the previous two years.

Applicant must have held a license in another state for the five-year period immediately preceding application, have engaged in active practice for at least five years, have passed a national board examination or equivalent and a clinical examination of equivalent merit, and have met continuing education requirements.
Reciprocity provisions to be established by administrative regulation; temporary licenses available for out-of-state dentists providing care to indigent populations.

Reciprocity is expressly prohibited. Licensure by credentials is available for dentists holding a license in another state. Louisiana has also enacted the Interstate Dental and Dental Hygiene Licensure Compact for expedited licensure.

Dentist must have been lawfully in practice for at least five years in another state and present a certificate of registration and duration of practice from that state's board; the other state must require a degree of competency equal to that required in Massachusetts.

Applicant must have passed the ADLEX and Maryland Dental Jurisprudence Examination; OR for the 5 preceding years actively engaged in practicing dentistry at least 850 hours per year on average, passed an examination with a clinical component in another state, passed a comprehensive written ADEX examination, and passed the Maryland Dental Jurisprudence Examination. Must meet all other qualifications, hold a license in another state, not be under investigation or disciplined elsewhere, and not have previously failed the Maryland examination.

Applicant must be licensed in good standing in another jurisdiction and either hold a substantially equivalent license for at least 3 consecutive years, or demonstrate qualifications substantially similar to Maine requirements. Board may waive examination requirements.
Applicant must substantially meet Michigan requirements, hold a license in a state with substantially equivalent standards, and may need to appear personally before the board for an interview.

Applicant must have passed all components of the National Board Dental Examinations; been in active practice at least 2,000 hours within 36 months of the application date; currently hold a license in another state or Canadian province in good standing with no pending or final disciplinary action; be of good moral character; and meet other credentialing requirements specified in board rule.

Licensed in another state for at least 5 consecutive years immediately preceding application; qualifications at least equivalent to Missouri initial registration requirements; at least 21 years of age and good moral character. Board may require Missouri law exam and/or practical exam if prior licensure was denied, revoked, or suspended for incompetency.

Licensure by credentials requires: graduation from ADA-accredited dental school; active practice or full-time dental education for past 5 years; valid unrestricted license in a state with equivalent standards that grants reciprocity to MS licensees; endorsements from all states; no pending/final disciplinary action; passed state or regional clinical exam within 5 years; never failed MS board exam; passed all National Board Examinations; passed written jurisprudence examination; payment of fee. Military applicants and spouses may also qualify under Section 73-50-1.
Board must determine the other state's license standards are substantially equivalent to or greater than Montana standards, and there is no reason to deny the license under Montana law.

Applicant must have required education, training, and qualifications; be in good standing; have passed satisfactory examinations; have a DDS or DMD from a CODA-accredited program; have been actively practicing for minimum 5 years; no pending or final disciplinary actions; no failed NC Board examinations; complete Jurisprudence and Sterilization and Infection Control exams.

Applicant must have been licensed in good standing and actively practicing dentistry in another jurisdiction with substantially equivalent requirements for at least five years immediately preceding application; must deliver certificates from all licensing jurisdictions; must pass the North Dakota jurisprudence examination; must meet any additional board requirements; and must pay applicable fees. Alternatively, may qualify with good standing, a board-approved hand skills examination, and substantially similar qualifications/education/experience.

Must meet board standards under section 38-126 and have been actively engaged in the practice of dentistry for at least one year under a license in another state, territory, or D.C. Practice in an accredited school or college of dentistry for a postgraduate or residency program also counts as active practice.
Requirements or standards for licensure in the other state must be equivalent to or greater than New Hampshire's requirements.

Applicant must have been licensed and practiced dentistry in another state for at least 5 years, present proof by affidavit, present a certificate from the other state's dental board certifying competency and good moral character, the certificate must be presented within 6 months of its issue date, and the other state must recognize NJ certificates in like manner.

Expedited license (no examination required) available if the applicant holds a current and in-good-standing license in another jurisdiction; board must process within 30 days. A general license by credentials may also be issued without clinical examination to an applicant duly licensed by clinical examination in another state/territory, with all licenses in good standing for 5 years prior to application and no board actions or pending proceedings during that period.

Applicant must hold a valid unrestricted license in another state/territory/DC, possess substantially similar qualifications, have not been disciplined or had a license revoked/suspended/refused, not have pending disciplinary action, pay applicable fees, and submit fingerprints for background check. Nevada also provides specific pathways via temporary license (NRS 631.272), restricted geographical license (NRS 631.274), and specialist's license by endorsement (NRS 631.255).

Applicant must file an application, meet educational requirements per commissioner's regulations, have satisfactory experience per board, pass an examination satisfactory to the board, be at least 21, be a US citizen or lawful permanent resident, and be of good moral character. Prior disciplinary history in another jurisdiction may result in denial.

Applicant must hold a license to practice dentistry in another state, or have satisfactory work experience, a government certification, or a private certification in a state that does not issue that license, in accordance with Chapter 4796 of the Revised Code. A jurisprudence examination may also be required.

Dentist must hold a general dentist license in good standing in another state, have practiced at least 500 hours within the previous 5 years, have passed a substantially equivalent regional examination, provide a letter of good standing from all states ever licensed in, and pass the Oklahoma jurisprudence examination.
Applicant must have engaged in active practice of dentistry in other states for at least 3,500 hours in the five years immediately preceding application and meet all other requirements for licensure.
Standards of the other state, territory, or Canada must be equal to PA standards; and such other jurisdiction must reciprocally recognize PA licenses.

Available for military members and spouses relocating to RI under military orders, where the other state's requirements are substantially equivalent. General reciprocity/endorsement is not separately enumerated in the dentistry chapter; military-member endorsement is available under Chapter 5-88.

The board may grant licenses via reciprocity to licensees of member regional testing services without further examination. Additionally, license by credentials is available for dentists actively practicing for at least 5 years, with a current out-of-state license, 70 hours of CE over past 5 years, no disciplinary actions, no felony convictions, and passing a jurisprudence exam.

Applicant must have graduated from a CODA-accredited US dental school with a DDS or DMD, be currently active with at least 3,000 dental clinical hours within the preceding five years, passed a standardized national comprehensive exam and a clinical regional or national exam, currently hold a valid license in another state, have no pending disciplinary actions, the other state's licensure requirements must be the same or higher than SD's, provide good moral character references, and pass the SD laws and rules examination.

Applicant must currently hold a valid license in another state, have no pending disciplinary charges, have not failed a Tennessee licensure exam, graduated from an ADA-CODA accredited school, demonstrate intent to practice or teach in Tennessee, and have practiced or taught for at least 2-5 years in another state depending on pathway.

Applicant must be licensed in good standing in another state with substantially equivalent requirements; graduated from CODA-accredited school; passed a national or board-recognized examination; passed Texas jurisprudence examination; submitted CPR certification; practiced for at least 3 years (or 5 years as dental educator); endorsed by home state board; and met any additional criteria by board rule.

Applicant must be currently licensed in good standing with an unrestricted license in another jurisdiction, document having met all licensure requirements except the degree requirement, and document having been successfully engaged in clinical practice as a dentist for not less than 6,000 hours in the five years immediately preceding application.

Must meet standard licensure requirements, hold a current unrestricted license in another US jurisdiction, be in good standing, not have committed grounds for denial, and have been in continuous clinical practice for five out of the six years immediately preceding application.

Applicant must be currently licensed in good standing in a US or Canadian jurisdiction with substantially equivalent requirements, complete an approved emergency office procedures course, pass the dentist jurisprudence examination, and meet active practice requirements. Where requirements are not substantially equivalent, 5 years of full-time practice (min 1,200 hrs/yr) and other conditions apply.

Applicant must hold a valid license and be currently engaged in practice in another state; must be a graduate of an approved dental school OR have practiced at least 4 years in another state plus completed a 1-year postdoctoral residency approved by the commission; may also be required to file documentation and demonstrate knowledge of Washington law.
Applicant must meet requirements established by the examining board by rule, submit evidence of current CPR/AED proficiency, present the out-of-state license, and pay the applicable fee.

Applicant must be currently licensed in at least one other state in the same discipline at the same practice level, license must be in good standing, must have passed required exams in the other state, no revocations or pending discipline, must pay applicable fees, no disqualifying criminal history, and must complete a clinical hand-skills exam as required for professions regulated by 30-4-1 et seq.

Applicant must hold a relevant, active license in good standing from another state with substantially equivalent or more stringent educational, training, examination and experience requirements; must demonstrate competency; must not have grounds for refusal/suspension/revocation; and must complete application procedures and pay fees. Note: 33-1-120(d)(ii) exempts professions with prescriptive drug authority from this section — dentists hold prescriptive authority so this general reciprocity provision may not apply; however, military expedited licensure is available under 33-1-117.

fields.rationale: The definitions cluster around five recognizable drafting patterns: the ADA model language ('evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, treatment... oral cavity, maxillofacial area... impact on the human body'); older 'performs or holds out' enumeration lists; 'healing art' framing; 'represents oneself / holds out' standards without the ADA body-impact clause; and one state with a near-circular definition.

assignments.raw_value: A person engages in the practice of dentistry who performs or holds out to the public as being able to perform dental operations; diagnoses, treats, operates on, corrects, attempts to correct, or prescribes for a disease, lesion, pain, injury, deficiency, deformity, or physical condition, malocclusion or malposition of the human teeth, alveolar process, gingiva, maxilla, mandible, or adjacent tissues
Any person shall be deemed to be practicing dentistry who does any of the following: (1) Performs, or attempts or professes to perform, any dental operation or dental service of any kind...

The evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment by nonsurgical, surgical, or related procedures of diseases, disorders, and conditions of the oral cavity, maxillofacial area, and the adjacent and associated structures and their impact on the human body

the practice of dentistry is the diagnosis, surgical or nonsurgical treatment and performance of related adjunctive procedures for any disease, pain, deformity, deficiency, injury or physical condition of the human tooth or teeth, alveolar process, gums, lips, cheek, jaws, oral cavity and associated tissues of the oral maxillofacial facial complex, including removing stains, discolorations and concretions and administering botulinum toxin type A and dermal fillers to the oral maxillofacial complex for therapeutic or cosmetic purposes.

Dentistry is the diagnosis or treatment, by surgery or other method, of diseases and lesions and the correction of malpositions of the human teeth, alveolar process, gums, jaws, or associated structures; and such diagnosis or treatment may include all necessary related procedures as well as the use of drugs, anesthetic agents, and physical evaluation.

"Dentistry" means the evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, or treatment, including nonsurgical, surgical, or related procedures, of diseases, disorders, or conditions of the oral cavity, maxillofacial area, or the adjacent and associated structures and the impact of the disease, disorder, or condition on the human body so long as a dentist is practicing within the scope of the dentist's education, training, and experience and in accordance with applicable law.

The practice of dentistry or dental medicine is defined as the diagnosis, evaluation, prevention or treatment by surgical or other means, of an injury, deformity, disease or condition of the oral cavity or its contents, or the jaws or the associated structures of the jaws.

"Practice of dentistry" is defined as the evaluation, diagnosis, prevention and treatment (nonsurgical, surgical or related procedures) of diseases, disorders and conditions of the oral cavity, maxillofacial area and the adjacent and associated structures and their impact on the human body provided by a dentist within the scope of the dentist's education, training and experience, in accordance with the ethics of the profession and applicable law.

Dentistry means the healing art which is concerned with the examination, diagnosis, treatment planning, and care of conditions within the human oral cavity and its adjacent tissues and structures.
